# etunnel

> etunnel exposes a service running on your machine (localhost:3000, a CI runner, a container behind NAT) at a public HTTPS URL. The SDK client opens one outbound WebSocket to an etunnel server, receives a random subdomain with automatic TLS, and the server relays visitor requests to the local service. No signup for the anonymous tier (random subdomain, 4h lifetime, 1 Mbps); an API key adds a static subdomain, longer lifetime and 10 Mbps. 22 SDKs share one wire protocol; the server is a single self-hostable Go binary with ACME built in. Live deployment: wss://t.etun.uk/tunnel.

Quick start (Node >= 22): `npx @easytunnel/et-sdk 3000` prints `TUNNEL_URL: https://<sub>.t.etun.uk`. Go: `go get github.com/topcheer/etunnel/sdk` then `etunnel.Connect(ctx, etunnel.Options{Server: "wss://t.etun.uk/tunnel", LocalAddr: "127.0.0.1:3000"})`. Every SDK honours `ETUNNEL_SERVER`, `ETUNNEL_LOCAL`, `ETUNNEL_TOKEN`, `ETUNNEL_SUBDOMAIN`, `ETUNNEL_RECONNECT=0`.

Copy-paste prompt for coding agents: the "Give this to your AI agent" section of the README.

## Gotchas

- Only the Go SDK streams bodies and relays WebSocket (101) upgrades. Every other SDK is buffer-based: fine for webhooks, JSON APIs and dashboards; not for SSE, large uploads or WebSockets.
- The tunnel WebSocket refuses handshakes that carry a browser `Origin` header (HTTP 403); run SDKs server-side, not in a browser page.
- A static subdomain needs an API key (a free key allows one) and the name must be claimed on `/me` first; the server rejects unknown names with `subdomain_plan`.
- Reconnects replay a signed `resumeToken` (30-minute window) to keep the same subdomain; the server needs a stable `SESSION_SECRET` for that to survive a restart.
- Multi-target routing (`-route /api=127.0.0.1:8080,strip -route /=3000`, or the SDK's `routes` option) is client-side: longest prefix wins on segment boundaries, `strip` keeps the query string, no match answers 404.
- Match server errors on the `code` field of the `error` message (`subdomain_taken`, `limit_reached`, `too_many_tunnels`, `unauthorized`, ...), never on the message text.
- Registry status differs per SDK at the current version; check the "Install" column of sdks/README.md before recommending a package (TypeScript, Kotlin, Scala, Perl, HarmonyOS, C and C++ are source-only; npm 1.7.35 and earlier are broken).
